items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The musicians were Billy Taylor Sr. (bass), Harry Dial (drums), Gene Cedric (clarinet & tenor) and myself.

ctx.x: One day I was contacted by Billy Taylor to do a recording date with Fats Waller. The Victor recording company had their studios in Camden, New Jersey, so the trip was made by train from New York to Philadelphia and Philly to Camden. Fats had two bottles of Whisky which we drank between New York and Philadelphia and he bought two more before we taken the train to Camden. Fats was really the most happy of lucky person I ever knew and he did not ask any of us for a cent to help him buy the whisky and when he taken a…

The musicians were Billy Taylor Sr. (bass), Harry Dial (drums), Gene Cedric (clarinet & tenor) and myself. The recordings got off to a good start and Fats ad-libed on all the singing numbers as though he had been playing and swinging them all his life and he had not seen any of them before they were given to him in the studio. The numbers were chosen by the recording company and not by himself.

Before each number was recorded, Fats would run it down on the piano and then we would go over it a couple of times to set the solos and get the idea about what riff Cedric and I were going to play in certain spots.
